speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The far right in France is now getting into power, too.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Because when you allow such free-flowing expressions without any kind of legal framework, what is going to happen?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: What will be the identity politics in Singapore?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Why do you want to vote for that Malay or that Indian?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Why do not we look at what we have and objectively ask, is it better than what is there elsewhere?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Is our situation better than what you see in the US, in Europe and in many Asian countries?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If the answer is yes, what has worked.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I have listed the things that have worked.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Perhaps, it will always be work-in-progress because of the deep-seated human emotions.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And I think it is very pertinent then to say how are the demographics working out.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I think that is something that should be looked at.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But the answer then is not to jump immediately to models which have failed miserably everywhere else.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The answer is to say, how do we reach these people.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: How do we get them to come and talk?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: These so-called curated fora, all it means is, a safe place is created, different people with different views come together.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It is hard-hitting, and it is on substance.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Nobody pulls their punches, but they are respectful.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That simply means that you are colonised in your minds.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I am not saying Mr Andre Low is, but I frequently read from, often foreigners, telling us, advising us on how we should run our country, and among that would be you should not have all these laws.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I say, look at yourself first before you prescribe to me.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But before that, I would like to thank the Minister for his speech where he mentioned the historical fact that the Malay is being offered land back in the 1960s and none has actually gone over during the 1960s.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I think it that sort of brings out the fact about our older generation of the Malay community being part of the Singapore's identity.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I have been hearing the issue about what the Leader of the Opposition has mentioned.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I find it hard to believe that the Leader of the Opposition is somewhat suggesting that the Vice Chairman Mr Faisal Manap did not know who Mr Deros is and what were the implications of his endorsement, given that his reach is quite significant online and his positions have been quite clear.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And I think it is on both sides – the PAP Malay MPs and of course, the WP Malay MPs, would know Mr Deros back then.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, my clarification is somewhat related to that, in some ways in terms of the guidelines and framework.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can the Minister share a bit more about the guidelines and framework pre- and, I think, because the situation happened during the heat of the GEs, how can we be more clear, going forward, in terms of how the guidelines and framework that he has shared.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And I truly support the fact that having a very clear guideline and framework as he has shared during his Ministerial Statement, will go a long way in in bringing a bit more clear direction into how we should deal with issues in relation to race and religion going forward.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Listening carefully to Mr Pritam Singh, he does not say Mr Faisal Manap did not know.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: He does not say that the WP Malay/Muslim candidates did not know.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, anyway, it is obvious that they know about Mr Deros.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I think Mr Pritam Singh agrees it should have been responded to clearly.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In terms of the framework and guidelines, there is one set of hard framework and guidelines in the law.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Then, there is common sense and the way we have applied.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And frankly, it has not been too bad in Singapore.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Most people have kept to that framework of one of trying to achieve consensus, trying to achieve a common ground and increase the common space.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And in my speech, I have given some indicators.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: You do not need to pull back on the substance, but remember, it is a multiracial society, you have demands, others have demands too.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Think about it and then see what is a give-and-take approach.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But that does not mean you ought to allow yourself to be discriminated against.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: You should not agree or keep quiet when there is racism.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But in terms of demands for the community, what do you want?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And if you leave it for a free-for-all, the domination will be by the majority community.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, we need politicians to be actually in there as leaders to try and give a framework, and bring good sense to these discussions and guide.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And not just politicians, but community leaders, religious leaders.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, in Singapore, a lot of that goes on, that constant linkage and the interactions between Government, community leaders, religious leaders, MPs on the ground.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But as Mr Low points out, some of the statistics for the younger generation are slightly different.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We will look at that, but there are many reasons for it, among which is the role of the Internet and external influences which are coming in, and people now forming tribes on the net among themselves and not forming relationships and communities on the ground.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And therefore, it becomes more difficult to reach out to them and get them to buy in into shared values, because their shared values are with their own net communities.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And also, with regard to the Malay community and as Ms Hazlina said and the Member have alluded to, I said they were the victims, meaning they were being the targets.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But they were bigger and they rose, they did not allow themselves to become victims.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They rose above it and they dealt with it.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: But as Member Saktiandi seems to suggest, I shared, publicly, the circumstances which relate to how Mr Noor Deros met up with certain WP candidates.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Mr Noor Deros himself, in a post on 6 May, says he was invited by an ustaz delegated by Mr Faisal Manap.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: This idea, just like the Minister says, we meet with people from all walks of life.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I believe there was a CNA article shortly after the elections.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Ministers Ong Ye Kung and Chee Hong Tat have no dealings with Fujian gang member, Su Haijin, says press secretaries, "As Ministers, they meet a diverse range of people at various events and gatherings." The key point to note is Mr Noor Deros has some views.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: He wants to advance a certain view of society.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I think we need to be very clear, Sir.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And then, during subsequent doorstops, Mr Singh made various statements about Deros being a nobody.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But Mr Singh can let me know if ever there was a rejection of Deros's endorsement of WP's candidates, a clear rejection.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: That would be correct, because that was what was said.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: But the point that I made early on before this exchange is, it was quite unequivocal in my understanding.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: By the time the matter came to a head at the Tampines rally, the statements that were made, I think, it was very clear where we stood on involvement of race or religion in politics.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: If somebody comes along and says, "I am of a certain race, and WP should support us because we are taking certain identity politics type of arguments forward." We will reject those, as we have to.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I am glad to hear that, except that it was not done for this election.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: He rejected PAS' endorsement, but he never rejected – neither WP nor Mr Singh ever rejected – Deros' endorsement of WP's Malay candidates, nor quite crucially, Deros' endorsement of Mr Faisal Manap for Tampines.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: This is an extract of a question that was asked to me during the doorstop.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And the Minister can take a view whether WP rejected what Mr Deros was proposing.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The question was, "We saw the post that WP has put up this morning" – this is from the journalist – "regarding foreign interference and regarding the WP's Muslim candidate meeting with the Malaysian activist, Noor Deros" – that is wrong, he is Singaporean – "so could you walk us through some details of the meeting?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: When did the meeting take place?" And then it goes on, "And was it part of the consideration that WP fielded Mr Faisal Manap in Tampines to meet with the Tampines MP Masagos?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Is it a coincidence that he is the Muslim Affairs Minister in this area?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Was the meeting part of the consideration following?” My reply, "No, absolutely not.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And of course, as our statement makes it quite clear, there is no situation of, I quote, 'if the WP pushes forward this agenda, I will support you.' I am sorry.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: We do not work politics like that in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: We do not work politics like that in Workers’ Party.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And I do not intend to repeat myself, but in the broad approach that the Minister is suggesting, going forward, in terms of ensuring that religion, race is not involved, or it does not mix with politics, we can agree with that.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And I think most sensible Singaporeans, and the vast majority of Singaporeans, I would add, would agree with that.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The Ministerial Statement today was about race or religion.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I want to pick up on a second point which Mr Low was alluding to.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I believe after the last elections, the ones before, in GE2020, a Minister himself came out to say that an older generation of Singaporeans has a certain approach with regard to race and religion; and a younger generation take a different approach.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Can I confirm with the Minister, is there a new framework that the Government is considering in view of this difference of approach in addressing race or religion issues?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Can we, for example, see more safe spaces or different style of trying to deal with race or religion issues, particularly for the reasons that the Minister states – the nature of social media and how a certain tribalism can develop in society?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I think, Sir, Mr Singh also knows what he said about PAS, when there was a clear and categorical rejection of PAS' endorsement, so I do not want to keep repeating myself.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: When it came to PAS, after the Prime Minister called for it, there was a clear rejection of the endorsement.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We unequivocally reject, and we do not need their support.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: When it came to Noor Deros, it was all about, "Well, it does not mean that we are going to carry on with his policies.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It does not mean who is he, and so on." But the crucial point is, it is very easy to have said "we reject".

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Anyway, I think the point has been made, but more important is what is for the future.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: As regards ways of engaging, what I would say is, what we have done so far has worked very well.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: At the same time, to say that we have achieved the best possible way of doing things is a road to disaster, because you need to be constantly alert to changing circumstances.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And we read the surveys, just as Mr Singh does and Mr Low does, and others do.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I do not necessarily agree with all the interpretations he puts forward.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But on many issues, demographically, there are different viewpoints, and it is important to analyse them carefully, not jump to conclusions.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: What are the reasons for these diverse viewpoints?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: On some issues, the younger people are more nationalistic and more Singaporean compared with older generations.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And we find that younger Singaporeans are less prone to foreign influence, compared with some demographics in the older generation.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, there are these variances and what influences are working on them.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Often, we find that these are influences from outside of Singapore.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, there are a variety of things that the Government is doing and also, is constantly analysing.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But we always welcome ideas on how we can do this better and if they are workable, we will consider.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: After two and a half hours, I believe all clarifications sought have been addressed by the Minister.
